record.paper_title: The Lieb-Thirring inequalities: recent results and open problems
record.original_question: For Jacobi matrices and discrete Schrödinger operators, determine what the correct analogue of the Lieb-Thirring inequality should be in the absence of scaling invariance, and then determine its optimal constants.

evidence.quote: Due to the lack of scaling invariance the form of the inequality and therefore also the question of optimal constants is less clear in this setting.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $J$ be a Jacobi matrix acting on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z})$ (or $\ell^2(\mathbb{N})$) of the form
$$(Ju)(n) = a_{n-1} u(n-1) + b_n u(n) + a_n u(n+1),$$
with real bounded sequences $\{a_n\}$ and $\{b_n\}$, and let $J_0$ denote the free Jacobi matrix corresponding to $a_n \equiv 1$, $b_n \equiv 0$, whose spectrum is $[-2,2]$. Equivalently, consider the discrete Schrödinger operator $H = -\Delta + V$ on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$, where $(\Delta u)(n) = \sum_{|m-n|=1}(u(m)-u(n))$ and $V:\mathbb{Z}^d 	o \mathbb{R}$ is a bounded potential.

Denote by $\{E_j^\pm\}$ the eigenvalues of $J$ lying outside (above $2$ or below $-2$ for) the spectrum of $J_0$, with distances to the spectrum $\delta_j^\pm := |E_j^\pm \mp 2|$ (and analogously for $H$ relative to the spectrum of $-\Delta$).

In the continuous setting, the classical Lieb–Thirring inequality asserts that for $\gamma \ge 0$ (with $\gamma > 1/2$ if $d=1$, $\gamma > 0$ if $d=2$, $\gamma \ge 0$ if $d \ge 3$),
$$\sum_j |E_j(-\Delta+V)|^\gamma \le L_{\gamma,d}\int_{\mathbb{R}^d} V_-(x)^{\gamma + d/2}\,dx,$$
and the central problems are to identify the sharp constants $L_{\gamma,d}$.

In the discrete setting, scaling invariance fails because the free operator has bounded spectrum, so the form of an analogous bound is not dictated by scaling. Determine:

(a) the correct formulation of a Lieb–Thirring-type inequality for Jacobi matrices and for discrete Schrödinger operators on $\ell^2(\mathbb{Z}^d)$, controlling an appropriate moment $\sum_j (\delta_j^\pm)^\gamma$ of the eigenvalue distances to the essential spectrum in terms of a suitable functional of the perturbation (or potential $V$);

(b) the optimal (sharp) constants in such an inequality, together with the extremizers (if any), for all admissible exponents $\gamma$ and dimensions $d$.
artifact.status_search_result: The discrete Lieb–Thirring problem is the subject of ongoing research. Various inequalities for Jacobi matrices and discrete Schrödinger operators have been proved (Hundertmark–Simon, Frank–Simon, and others), with improved constants obtained in subsequent works, but the sharp constants and even the canonical form of the inequality in the absence of scaling invariance remain not fully resolved. Recent works (e.g., 2025 preprints on optimal Lieb–Thirring-type inequalities for Schrödinger and Jacobi operators with complex potentials) continue to establish new optimal-type bounds in special regimes, indicating the problem is partially solved at best and broadly open.

status_evidence.title: New constants in discrete Lieb–Thirring inequalities for Jacobi matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Some results used for improving constants in the Lieb–Thirring inequalities for Schrödinger operators can be translated to discrete Schrödinger operators and Jacobi matrices.
status_evidence.claim: Improved but not sharp constants are available for discrete Lieb–Thirring inequalities.

status_evidence.title: Lieb–Thirring Inequalities for Finite and Infinite Gap Jacobi Matrices
status_evidence.snippet: Lieb–Thirring inequalities for Jacobi matrices with finite and infinite gap essential spectra.
status_evidence.claim: Form of the inequality continues to be investigated; multiple variants exist.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Lieb–Thirring type inequalities for Schrödinger and Jacobi operators with complex potentials
status_evidence.snippet: New optimal Lieb–Thirring-type inequalities for Jacobi operators with complex potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp constants are an active topic with new optimal results in 2025.
